content:
incident-bot: [P1] GPU pool 'fast-gpu' saturated — autoscaler at max nodes (24/24). Pending queue growing rapidly: ~125 requests pending. Incoming rate ~420 req/min. Paging on-call.
oncall-bot: @channel Paging: on-call (Maria G.) -> please acknowledge.
Maria G.: ack. I'm digging in now. brief handoff to Raj in 2m if needed. tagging infra and support.
Raj P.: I'm joining. quick status: autoscaler desired=24, max=24, current=24. Lots of Pending pods in redwood-prod: ~48 Pending, many in CrashLoopBackOff or PendingScheduling due to no GPU capacity.
Ken S.: any PDBs or taints preventing scaling? I don't see PDB blockers. node taints look normal for fast-gpu pool.
Sophie M.: customer-impact note: support queue spiking. Lina, can you surface top-3 affected tenants (by revenue/SLAs)?
Lina (Support): On it. Top-3: AcmeAnalytics (timeouts, 429s), Shoply (inference latency spikes), Synthia (large batch jobs queued). I've sent status alert to account leads and created temporary status page note.
Raj P.: attaching quick kubectl snapshot — pending pods are mostly model-serving replicas.
```
# kubectl -n redwood-prod get pods --field-selector=status.phase==Pending -o wide | head -n 60
NAME                                         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
model-bert-serve-7c6f9d9d-xxxxx               0/1     Pending   0          2m
model-llama-serve-6b5a8c8c-yyyyy               0/1     Pending   0          3m
... (48 Pending total)
```
Raj P.: autoscaler logs show scaling inhibited because current nodes == max_nodes (24). policy.max_nodes=24. Incoming spike exceeding scale rate.
Maria G.: options: 1) manual increase of node pool max (temporary), 2) evict lower-priority jobs / throttle non-SLAs, 3) route some requests to fallback smaller models. What do we want? :thinking_face:
Sophie M.: if we can bump quickly that's preferable. Routing to fallback increases error-rate risk for customers. Support prefers manual bump + careful communication.
Ken S.: I'll surface potential limits: cloud quota for GPUs, infractl operator permissions, and any open change windows. If quotas allow, we can raise to 30 for emergency.
Raj P.: I'm proposing manual cap raise to 30 nodes (temp), then scale back once backlog cleared. @Deploy Bot, initiate manual pool increase request.
Deploy Bot: Manual scale request received for pool 'fast-gpu' -> target 30. Approval required from infra operator oncall.
Ken S.: approving. Running infractl command now.
```
# infractl nodepool update --name fast-gpu --max-nodes 30 --target 30
Applying update to nodepool fast-gpu...
```
Deploy Bot: Update accepted, provisioning new nodes. Expected new nodes: 6. Estimated time to register: 3-7 minutes. Monitoring attach.
oncall-bot: provisioning metrics: new nodes registering: 0/6
(2 minutes later)
oncall-bot: provisioning metrics: new nodes registering: 3/6
Raj P.: good. starting to see Pending -> Running as Kube schedules pods onto new nodes. beginning to drain some lower-priority batch pods to free ephemeral resources.
Maria G.: turning on temporary routing to fallback model for low-priority tenant groups to reduce queue growth. small config change pushed to router.
```
# routerctl update-route --route inference-low --model fallback-small --traffic 100%
Applied.
```
Lina (Support): Notifying impacted tenants with ETA. AcmeAnalytics and Shoply acknowledged, Synthia asked to postpone large batches.
oncall-bot: provisioning metrics: new nodes registering: 6/6 -> all nodes joined.
Raj P.: cluster reports 30 nodes now. Pending backlog decreasing: 48 -> 16 in last 4m. Throttles reduced, 429 error rate down ~85%.
Sophie M.: customer impact update: Support sees success confirmations from AcmeAnalytics and Shoply. I'll keep monitoring for SLA breaches.
Ken S.: action item — we need to determine why autoscaler didn't pre-emptively increase: check scale-up policy rate limit and historical windows. Possible causes: burst exceeded scale rate or cloud API throttling.
Maria G.: agreed. For now incident mitigation succeeded. We're keeping the pool at 30 for 30 minutes then step it down gradually. @Raj P. can you coordinate rollback plan?
Raj P.: plan: schedule step-down to 26 after 30m observation, then 24 once stable. I'll create a rollback-runbook and a short changelog entry.
Deploy Bot: Note — manual nodepool change logged and requires follow-up ticket to infra for quota review and autoscaler tuning.
Maria G.: immediate post-incident tasks:
- confirm no customer data loss
- collect autoscaler logs + scale events
- run synthetic traffic tests to validate scale behavior
- schedule postmortem in SRE triage tomorrow
Ken S.: I'll capture cloud quota metrics and rate limits. Also will propose increasing autoscaler max_nodes or adjusting policies for burst windows during business hours.
Lina (Support): I'll follow up with impacted accounts and include timeline + mitigations. Also adding a brief to CS leadership.
(30 minutes after initial page)
oncall-bot: backlog now ~4 pending. throughput back to expected. 429s returned to baseline.
Maria G.: marking incident as mitigated. Leaving the temporary cap at 30 for monitoring, rollback plan scheduled. Handoff to morning oncall for post-incident review.
Raj P.: uploading logs and notes to /incidents/1779204321 in our Confluence / Incident repo. I'll own the postmortem.
Sophie M.: adding product impact note: recommend we model autoscaler behavior under larger burst profiles and add a protective routing rule to shed low-priority traffic earlier.
Ken S.: will create infra ticket to evaluate autoscaler rate limits and request permanent max increase or smarter policies.
Maria G.: thanks team. closing real-time coordination channel. We'll follow up with a full postmortem and remediation tasks. :white_check_mark:
